newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Tractor shrs end sluggish debut up.
newsitem.headline: First Tractor shrs end sluggish debut up.

text.p: Shares of Chinese agricultural tractor maker First Tractor Co Ltd disappointed investors by ending their trading debut near intraday lows on Monday, although they closed above their issue price, brokers said.

"It was disappointing because the stock failed to hold above our expected support level of about HK$5.50, though it once traded as high as above HK$6," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
The shares ended at HK$5.05, compared to their issue price of HK$4.50 each. They moved in a range from HK$4.975 to HK$6.10. Volume was 108.93 million shares worth HK$611.54 million.

"I think a level of about HK$5.50 is reasonable in reflecting the company's fundamentals," said Rachael Tsang, analyst at Vickers Ballas. "A generally weak market sentiment triggered profit-taking interest."

The crawler-tractor maker issued 300 million H-shares in a global offering. Of the total, 255 million shares were placed with international investors and 45 million shares were offered to the Hong Kong public.
The Hong Kong public offering was 296.4 times subscribed.
H-shares are shares of China-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong.

"Unlike red-chip stocks, H-shares lack the driving force of the asset injection concept and that was seen to be a factor dampening investors' buying interest for the sector as well as in this stock," Vickers' Tsang said.
Analysts generally still expected the stock to benefit from China's growing agricultural sector.
"I would recommend accumulating if the stock fall further as its earnings outlook is still seen to be very bright," Au said.
First Tractor said it would use the net proceeds to finance expansion of its manufacturing capacity, repay debt and for working capital.
